tagline.text: A members-only beach and nature club and golf course on Bataan's west coast in Morong

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,500~8,500 (from the official 2025 day-guest fee to one night in a room, 2017 data)

children.text: Anvaya Cove is a large seaside community developed by Ayala Land on the Morong coast on the west side of the Bataan peninsula, and it holds a members-only beach and nature club and an 18-hole golf course. Unlike an ordinary public beach, you get in by a member's invitation or a room reservation, so work out how you will visit before you go.

Anvaya Cove is a coastal residential and leisure estate in Barangay Mabayo, Morong, at the western edge of the Bataan peninsula. Forested hills wrap around a small cove facing the West Philippine Sea, and the estate was developed jointly by Ayala Land Premier and SUDECO. According to SUDECO, the whole estate covers about
620 hectares
. The official website explains that "Anvaya" means family in Sanskrit.
The first thing a traveler needs to know is that this is a
members-only

place. The Beach & Nature Club is presented as a membership facility even on the official website, and non-members can only enter by invitation from a member or by booking a club room or a condo inside the estate. In return, once you are inside you get a polished sand beach, an infinity pool, several restaurants and bars, a spa, a bike park and kids' facilities, all in one self-contained resort. The atmosphere is quite different from a crowded public beach.

The golf course is known separately. Anvaya Cove Golf and Sports Club is an 18-hole, par-72 course split into a mountain nine (Mountain Nine) and a seaside nine (Seaside Nine), with some holes laid out close to the beach. According to golf information sites it was designed by Kevin Ramsey of Golfplan, it was named Asia's best new course in 2014, and the SUDECO page says it was named Southeast Asia's most sustainable championship golf course in 2025. The course covers about 82 hectares.
It takes about
2.5 hours
by car from Manila (according to Ayala Land) and about
20–45 minutes

from the Subic Freeport. It is well placed for crossing over to Bataan as part of a Subic or Olongapo trip. However, it is not an attraction open to the general public, so please treat every price and rule in this guide as something to confirm directly with the club before you visit.

The club beach is open from around sunrise to sunset, with beach volleyball, frisbee and sandcastle building. Because it sits inside the cove the water is relatively calm, and at dusk the sun sets over the western sea in front of the Sunset Bar.
The swimming pool and infinity pool run daily from
to
according to the official information. Guest reviews report a jacuzzi beside the pool and changing rooms, showers, lockers and towels. Proper swimwear is required.
According to the official website, water sports run daily
(last call
), and kayaking, snorkeling, banana boat rides, water skiing and windsurfing are listed. Activities and fees depend on the weather and the season, so check at the lobby.
The bike park, with trails for riders from beginner to professional, is open daily
. True to the name "Nature Club," activity programs such as forest trails, bird watching, ziplines and climbing have been advertised.
Bamboo Café serves buffets and à la carte dishes from
until midnight. Pawikan Beach Bar & Grill on the beach is open
for grilled food and seafood by the sea, and drinks are available at the Tower Bar and the Sunset Bar.
Veda Spa inside the club is open Monday to Thursday
and Friday to Sunday and holidays
. Massages need a reservation, so it is safest to book as soon as you arrive.

This is an 18-hole course made up of the Seaside Nine on the beach side and the Mountain Nine on the hill side. It has a driving range and a clubhouse, and one source says tee-time reservations are taken by phone up to 7 days before the round. Weekends and holidays may be members only, so confirm in advance.

Seahorse Kiddie Village runs a supervised program for children aged 5 to 12. There are also a game lounge (Wii and PlayStation) and a library lounge, which makes it a good place to spend time with kids on a rainy day.

items.title: Day visit
items.subtitle: By member invitation or as a staying guest

children.text: Leave Manila early. The route Ayala Land recommends is NLEX to the San Fernando exit, then SCTEX and out at the Angeles exit.

Register at the main gate. You are known to receive a charge card instead of paying in cash, and what you spend is settled when you leave. Have the member's contact number, your reservation confirmation and your vehicle plate number ready.
Spend time at the beach and the pool. Outside food cannot be brought in, so the simplest option is the lunch buffet at Bamboo Café.
Try one water sport, such as kayaking or snorkeling. The last call is at
, so sign up in good time.
Watch the sunset at the Sunset Bar, then have dinner at Pawikan Beach Bar & Grill. The Sunset Bar is open only until
Settle your bill and head out. Reviews advise against driving out toward Subic at night because of the winding provincial road and the darkness.
A day pass often comes with the condition that a member must invite you. If you do not know a member, it is more realistic to book a room or a condo inside the estate, as in the overnight plan below.

items.title: 2 days, 1 night
items.subtitle: Relaxing in a beach club room

children.text: Check-in has been announced as 2 pm. Even if you arrive early you may be able to look around the club facilities before your room is ready, so ask when you book.
Walk around the infinity pool, the kids' facilities and the beach.
Watch the sunset at the Sunset Bar, then have dinner.
End the day at the game lounge, the library lounge or the spa.
The next morning, have the breakfast buffet at Bamboo Café, then try the bike park or a walk in the forest.
Check-out is at noon. Reviews say beach club use can be restricted on check-out day, so ask ahead.
Room rates and what is included vary a great deal with the season and the rules. Treat this plan as a rough guide to the flow of the stay.

items.title: From Manila by private car or rental car

children.text: It is said to take about
2.5–3 hours
from Manila. The route Ayala Land's official blog gives is NLEX to the San Fernando exit, transfer to SCTEX, and out at the Angeles exit.
Pass through the Subic Freeport and follow the coastal road toward Morong. It is about
25km
and
20–45 minutes
from Subic, and signs lead the way.
The road is winding and poorly lit, so try to arrive in daylight.
A day trip is possible, but the travel takes up a large part of the day.
The nearest international airport is Clark International Airport (CRK), and landing at Manila (NAIA) and continuing by vehicle is also common. Check the latest flight schedules.
Public transport from the airport to the club is not convenient, so arrange a rental car or a booked ride in advance.

items.title: Public transport and getting around locally

children.text: You can reach Morong town by public transport, but the connection to the estate gate should be checked locally, and a rental car or booked ride is far more convenient.
Inside the estate, reviews say you can ask reception for an electric golf cart driven by club staff.
If the beach and the pools are your goal, the dry season from November–May is best. The west coast of Bataan is most comfortable when there is little rain and the sea is calm.

In the June–October rainy season, rain and strong waves can limit water sports. On the other hand it is the low season with cheaper rooms, and indoor facilities and the spa are still enjoyable. During super-peak periods such as Holy Week, Christmas and All Saints' Day, some free-entry perks reportedly do not apply and a per-person entrance fee is charged, so avoid these periods or ask in advance.

The club's rooms are casitas spread around the estate, in four types: Anvaya Suite, Lagoon Terrace, Garden Terrace and Garden Room. The Garden Terrace is described as having a king-size bed and a forest view, and the Garden Room as a room beside the forest with twin beds and pull-out beds. Check-in is known to be at 2 pm and check-out at noon. Separately, you can also rent a privately owned condo or house in the Tower Complex inside the estate, though it sits a fair walk from the beach club.

Eating inside the club is the default. Bamboo Café has Southeast Asian–themed buffets and weekend live stations, and Pawikan Beach Bar & Grill is an open-air restaurant on the beach. Italian and Mediterranean dishes are described at Tap-In Bar and Café. Outside food and drinks cannot be brought in, and you pay with a charge card instead of cash, with credit cards also accepted.
Before you go, always confirm the latest entry and guest rules with the club. The official website lists the phone number (02) 7793-9000 and the email members@anvayacove.com.

The rule that a member must accompany guests on weekends and holidays has long been reported, and one review says a member's authorization letter alone was not accepted. Weekday visits are more flexible.
Print your reservation confirmation and tell security your vehicle plate number in advance. Non-members should carry the member's contact number so the club can verify the visit.
Reports say you leave a government-issued ID at the gate and receive a charge card, so bring your ID.
Many reviews say the Wi-Fi inside the club is weak. Bring a pocket Wi-Fi or a data plan, and save your itinerary offline.
Pets, drivers and bodyguards in the beach club, and outside food are reportedly restricted.
Proper swimwear is required in the pools. Towels and shower supplies are provided by the club.
Golf reservations are made by phone up to 7 days before the round, and one source says the course closes on Tuesdays for maintenance, so confirm.
This is not an open public beach. If you arrive without a member's invitation or a room reservation you may be refused entry, so be sure to confirm in advance.
The day-guest fee is from the club's official 2025 rate sheet (effective 1 Feb 2025); the room, gym, corkage and other prices are 2017–2018 data. Ask the club for the current rates.
During super-peak periods (Holy Week, Christmas, All Saints' Day and public holidays) free-entry perks may not apply and a per-person entrance fee may be charged, according to some listings.
Some accommodation listings say the beach club cannot be used on check-out day and only the condo pool is available. Check the booking conditions.
The estate is large and the roads wind, so take care when driving at night.
Water activities may be limited in the rainy and typhoon seasons, so check the weather ahead of time.
A freeport about
20–45 minutes
away by car, where you can combine a marine park and shopping.
A facility in Morong where local residents protect olive ridley sea turtles; "Pawikan" in the club's name means sea turtle. Check opening hours locally.

blocks.title: Our Lady of the Pillar Church

children.text: The parish church of Morong, founded by the Augustinian Recollects in 1607, where you can get a short look at Morong's history.
The provincial capital of Bataan, on the eastern side of the peninsula, and a good base for a Bataan itinerary.
